High end restaurant in Hanoi
Dec 2019 • Family
High end restaurant specialising in seafood seriously lacks lustre in its dishes. However, it has redeeming features for some of its seafood notably the Claypot live prawns, scallops deep fried salted eggs soft shell crabs. We decided to give the fish a miss as it was around 1.3kg, a tad too big for us. The cuttlefish in spicy lemongrass was rejected as it was hard to chew and has the consistency of chewing gum. The manager was gracious in acknowledging that the fish was not y expectations and agreed to take it off the list. Service quality at least is to be appreciated as it was excellent despite the fact that the staff could not speak English.

Apart from seafood, we tried the Stir fried Beef with capsicums (bell peppers) which comes with French fries; san ho fried noodles and asparagus which wasn’t bad!

Surprisingly, we had a live performance from 3 ladies playing instrumental Vietnamese songs. Overall, one has to be selective with choosing the food and getting more feedback on the better dishes to try.

Smart, Reasonable Food, Poor Service
Sep 2019
We came across San Ho by chance while in Hanoi in late September and stepped in for lunch.

We were the only clients in the main restaurant area that day although we had a sense there were some customers in a separate function room.

The restaurant is very smart with a modern decor. It seemed to actually be in the throes of a redecoration. 

The food was focused mainly on a seafood theme and we had two mains. They were nice enough but not any more outstanding than other reasonable restaurants we visited in Vietnam.

While there were a number of staff in evidence and they were smartly dressed the service was very slow and frankly they seemed to be largely disinterested. Three of them disappeared into another area chattering away when a friend, or perhaps a former member of staff came in with a young child.

It was a curious and disappointing experience.

Disappointing experience
Aug 2019
A key test to visit a restaurant is to go alone. Since I travel for my work, I often appear alone in a restaurant and ... what happens next is a test in hospitality. Table next to toilet, kitchen, cleaning up table, kin a corner, far away ... This is what happened again in this restaurant. I was put on the first floor in a lonely corner, next to a screen to hide a passage and next to the cleaning up table. Service was swift but as impersonal as can be. No thank you, no welcome, no how are you. Even not a question whether the food was nice or good or tasty. The food was strange: crab with a French onion sauce ... A nice spicy soup but with a chewy tiger prawn and finally a tiger prawn with rice. Alas the grilled prawn was overcooked and dry. I think the overall cold atmosphere did not add up to the experience: cleaning up background noise, cutlery being thrown in drawers, cleaning ladies swiping the floor in front of you ... Even when I paid nobody watched me, neither talked to me. In the end, I asked whether I could make a remark. I repeated the question twice since they even did not hear my question. So I mentioned next that nobody had ever asked me a word about the food experience .. I got a million apologies .... I paid he bill and I left. So maybe, it was because I was alone. Maybe that a group or family would be received better. Bu, I have to say that I DO NOT recommend this restaurant; neither for the food and neither for the atmosophere.

Enjoyed our dinner very much
Nov 2017 • Couples
We visited for dinner on a Wednesday evening. It wasn’t very busy but we really enjoyed the food. We had simmered salmon and bacon in clay pot and pork and shrimp in clay pot. We also chose the baked seafood rice in pineapple and a couple of other vegetable dishes so it was quite a feast for two. There was traditional live music which was a nice unexpected extra. The restaurant is spread over a few floors and rooms and the staff were very attentive. It’s a bit on the pricey side but they do take credit cards. We would definitely visit again if we were in Hanoi longer. There was a complimentary appetiser and tea at the end of the meal.

Duterte wuz here
Oct 2017 • Business
Whatever your opinion of the man, he knows good seafood.

His picture adorns the front staircase leading up to an almost MC Escher layout - not in a bad way. Many restaurants have multi tiered extensions built out from old Colonial buildings.

They've a 1.5m VND set dinner which was quite good. The set meal is not so much Vietnamese only styles but more of a mixture of French lobster/Chinese sharks' fin/Japanese abalone, etc.

There is also land-lubbing fare for creatures which don't eat sea bugs.

Wine selection was balanced, not exceptional but more than satisfactory for most palettes.

Service was very good and they've a live Vietnamese three string band in the lobby playing traditional and contemporary songs. 

Nothing like listening to Bruno Mars on an Erhu while you're busting lobster claws.

pricey but good quality seafood
Jun 2017 • Family
We visited the Hoa Lo prison nearby at 11am and couldn't withstand the heat, so came to this restaurant for lunch which was only a few minutes away. The service was excellent as we had almost our personal waitress. Food was also of very high quality, especially the lobster porridge that they recommended after we ordered a 1.2kg lobster. Oysters with cheese and lobster with cheese were likewise very nicely made - only rather pricey, so better double check the price when ordering seafood as the costs are written per 100g on the menu.
